limitations.text: An HPO annotation is a clinical observation recorded in a cohort, not a mechanism.
Annotation coverage is uneven: rare diseases are annotated densely, common diseases barely.
The release writes disease identifiers in OMIM and Orphanet; the MONDO cross-reference table is the release's own mapping, and an identifier absent from it stays unmapped.
A gene annotation's disease column names the disease it was recorded in, so a gene-phenotype row can restate a target-disease association; the project records that overlap rather than hiding it.

purpose.text: Give a disease the phenotypes its patients were recorded with, and give a gene the phenotypes its variants were recorded with, so that a reader can reach a disease through the body rather than only through a target-disease row.

profile.coverage: every disease and gene the release annotates
